description.value:
"The land is not scenery. The land is a person. You are the version of it that finally stood up and walked over to complain."

You are not descended from the land. You are the land. A hex decided to become a person and the person is you. The standing stones on the ridge are distant cousins. The bedrock under the bunker is a grandparent. Mortals call you a Hex-Giant. You don't correct them.

Creature Type. Humanoid (Menhirkin). Size. Medium, but you count as Large for carrying capacity and the size of creatures you can shove or grapple. Speed. 6 squares

Heartstone (passive). A fragment of your home hex is literally inside you. While in any hex your Domain controls or has claimed: reroll the lowest die on Body checks, and you cannot be forcibly removed from the hex against your will (teleportation, banishment, forced march) without first being reduced to 0 Integrity.

Land Memory (1/Soma Break). Lay a hand on any surface older than you; the GM tells you one true thing the land remembers.

Living Rampart (1/Soma Break). Reaction — when a creature you can see targets an ally adjacent to you with an attack, the attacker rolls 3d10 keep lowest 2 on that attack roll.

Stonebound (passive). Reroll the lowest die on Body checks to resist being pushed, knocked Prone, or otherwise forcibly moved. Reroll the lowest die on Body checks to build, repair, or fortify structures, siegeworks, and defensive emplacements.

Domain Edge. Your Domain gains +20 Violence marks and +20 Non-Lethal marks at campaign start.

description.value:
“Some stone was born yelling.”

Menhirkin (Igneous). You are new rock. The Shattering was your birthday. The land that stood up and began answering chose you because it wanted a mouth that remembered being molten. You run hot, you cool slow, and you are, structurally, still furious about something.

Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid (Menhirkin).
  • Size. Medium.
  • Movement. 6 squares walking.
  • Lineage Lean. Menhirkin does not grant fixed attribute bonuses; your background handles increases. Your heritage leans toward Violence in fiction and through Tier powers.

Menhirkin Core: The Land Stood Up

Shared across all Menhirkin heritages. Granted at character creation via the base ancestry item.

  • Stone Soul. You count as Large for carry, shove, and grapple despite your Medium frame. You reroll the lowest die on checks to resist being forcibly moved.
  • Hex Recognition. Once per scene, while you are on a natural surface you are directly touching, you may whisper a single question about the place. The GM answers with one true thing the land knows.
  • Slow to Wear. You reroll the lowest die on Body checks against Stress, long-duration physical wear, forced marches, climate exposure, and sustained labor. You do not tire the way softer things tire.
  • Heavy Presence. Your weight and settledness are perceptible. Creatures within 2 squares of you know you are there even if they cannot see you; you roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 on Intrigue (Stealth) checks unless you are on or in stone.

Igneous Traits

  • Heat Memory. When you take thermal damage with the fire flavor, you may bank that damage. Before your next Soma Break, you may spend the banked heat as a bonus action to add +1d10 exploding thermal damage (flavor: fire) to your next weapon attack, unarmed strike, or grapple that connects.
  • Molten Bearing. You count fire, smoke, ash, and heated terrain as normal ground for the purposes of difficult terrain and footing. Contact with your bare skin singes paper and warms metal.

Domain Edge

  • Domain Edge. Your Domain gains +20 Violence marks and +20 Non-Lethal marks at campaign start.

description.value:
"Set your feet. The line forms on you."

The Bulwark is the wall — and the wall runs on Surge, like everyone, but yours arrives the hard way: every time you take Integrity damage you bank +1 Surge (max +2/round (+3 with Polarity Mastery, Mountain)). You eat the blow and turn it into the power to anchor, erupt, or hold. At zero Surge you still stand in the way; soak one hit and your turn opens up.

The Fortress (spent via Surge — Bulwark only)

  • Brace Wall (1) — you and adjacent allies gain DR equal to Tier this round.

  • Bulwark Stance (6) — adjacent allies share your defenses until your next turn.

  • Anchor (5) — you and one ally become immune to forced movement and crowd-control until next round.

  • Mass Aegis (8) — allies within Tier squares gain +Tier to every defense this round.

  • Sanctum (9) — immune to one damage type for a round.

  • Mythic Stand (10) — invulnerable until the start of your next turn.

These were always the Bulwark's birthright; they no longer leak into everyone else's menu. The old Frame and Ruin tricks are Surge spends too — Absorb (1), Push (1), Shockwave Footing (2), Catastrophic Entry (3), Siege Works (2) and Ruin to Renewal (3) — and your Path adds three more of its own.

description.value:
The world has two ways of saying no to change. You learn one of them today.

On gaining Bulwark Initiation 1 you receive:

  • Skill rank +1 in Athletics (Violence).

  • Skill rank +1 in Melee and Plating.

  • +30 Violence marks to your Domain's cap, and 20 marks of free siege works folded into the buffer every time your Domain opens or joins a Siege.

  • You bank Surge by eating the blow: +1 Surge each time you take Integrity damage (max +2 a round). Spend it from the ◆ Surge menu.

Your Path's L1 feature shapes how you bank it.

description.value:
"Something gives way. You aim where."

Doctrine: Controlled eruption — trade stability for force on purpose.

The Cataclyst is the wall that decides to come down on someone. Your Surge spends turn your own stored impact into offense: a strike that erupts, a seam found in anything, a moment where the ground itself gives up standing still.

Path (spent via Surge)

  • Erupt (1) — your next Strike blazes (+Tier d6 exploding) and hurls the target back.
  • Shatter (3) — your next Strike ignores resistances; the target is Staggered.
  • Cataclysm (5) — your next Strike lands as a max-die crit, and foes in reach are knocked Prone.

The world pushes. You remain.

Rules

description.value:
The hinge swings either way. You decide which way every turn.

At the start of each of your turns, declare a stance for the round — Advance or Anchor.

  • Advance. Your offensive path spends (Erupt, Shatter, Cataclysm) cost 1 less this round (minimum 1), and you gain +2 squares of movement.

  • Anchor. You cannot be moved against your will until the start of your next turn, and Absorb's cap rises by 1d4.

You may change stance once during your turn as a free action — declare again.

description.value:
Breach Specialist

Everything has a seam. Most people just don’t look.

Rules

You gain a rank in Tinkering. If you already have it, its rank rises by one instead.

When you hit an object, door, barrier, or construct with a weapon attack, you may treat the attack as dealing maximum damage to the target’s objects-only resistances (GM adjudication). Once you do, you can’t do so again until the start of your next turn.

⚙ +1 Tinkering. 🃏 Card — the max-damage-vs-objects rider, once per round.

description.value:
Signature move. Once a scene, you choose which kind of inevitability you are.

Anchor or Advance — 1/scene (recovers on Soma Break). As part of any action on your turn, declare a stance. The chosen stance lasts until the end of your next turn:

  • Anchor. You cannot be moved against your will by any effect short of a Heroic-DC (22) push from a creature of your size or larger. Forced movement, knockback, teleportation targeting you, banishment, and dimensional swap effects all fail.

  • Advance. You cannot be prevented from reaching a destination you declare on the same action. Difficult terrain, conditions that halve speed, reaction strikes, and zone-of-control effects do not stop your movement toward that point. You may still take damage along the way.

Doctrine features at L5+ extend or modify which stance you favor.

system.source: Bad Eden Core Feats v1 (2024 rules)

description.value:
Calculated Risk

You open yourself on purpose.

Rules

Once per turn, you may choose to reroll the lowest die on an attack roll. If you do, attack rolls against you reroll the lowest die until the start of your next turn.

🃏 Card — once per turn: banks a reroll for your attack; attacks against you reroll their lowest die until your next turn (GM applies).

One. Or the other. Not both. Decide.

Decide The Weather — 1/scene (recovers on Soma Break). As an action, spend 4 Surge. Choose one of the two effects:

  • Wall. Raise a wall of hardened debris in a 6 squares long, 2 squares high line on a contiguous surface within 1 square of you. The wall is impassable until the end of your next turn (it absorbs damage normally; treat as Hard hardness DC 18). Creatures occupying the line at the moment of casting are pushed 1 square to one side and may make a Body defense check (DC 15 + Initiation tier) — failure leaves them prone.
  • Rubble. Collapse a standing structure within 6 squares (door-sized to building-segment-sized — GM call) into rubble. The resulting rubble field grants your allies cover when within it. Enemies attempting to move through the rubble field roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 on movement-related attribute checks until the rubble is cleared (1 minute of dedicated work or another action with sufficient force).

“Power is not rage. Power is what still obeys you after the world breaks.”

Archetype (Bad Eden): Violence (Warlord). Commander, breaker, disciplined engine of force. You do not merely hit hard — you make force coherent.

Archetype Effects

  • Faction Edge. Your Domain earns +10 Violence marks each turn while you serve it.

  • Tier Engine. See this Archetype’s Tier feats (Tier 1–4) for the full tactical and strategic expression of battlefield command, violent pressure, and military dominance.
